title: Tally Two-by-Two Tiles by Dark Cells
statement:
A grid has m rows and n columns, and every cell is light except the ones listed in dark. Each entry [x, y] marks the cell in row x and column y as dark. No cell is listed twice.

A tile is any 2 × 2 square of cells inside the grid; there are (m − 1) · (n − 1) of them, and they overlap. Return an array tally of length 5 where tally[i] is the number of tiles that contain exactly i dark cells.

The grid can be huge, but the list of dark cells is short.

examples.why: There are 4 tiles. The corner cell lies in only the top-left one.
The centre cell lies in all four tiles. A cell can belong to up to four tiles, so counting per cell is not enough.
The three tiles, left to right, hold 2, 3 and 1 dark cells.

hints: With up to ten billion tiles you cannot look at each one. Which tiles can possibly hold a dark cell?
A dark cell (x, y) is inside at most four tiles: the ones whose top-left corner is (x−1..x, y−1..y), as long as the tile fits in the grid.
Count dark cells per tile in a hash map keyed by the tile's top-left corner. Every tile in the map goes to tally[count]; all the rest go to tally[0].

explain.intuition:
Most tiles are completely light, and you never need to visit them. Only tiles that touch a dark cell are interesting, and each dark cell touches at most four. So flip the question around: instead of asking each tile how many dark cells it has, let each dark cell vote for the tiles it belongs to.

Name a tile by its top-left corner. Cell (x, y) belongs to the tiles with corners (x−1, y−1), (x−1, y), (x, y−1) and (x, y), minus those that would stick out of the grid. A hash map from corner to vote count gives every non-empty tile's dark count. Tiles never mentioned have zero dark cells, so tally[0] is the total number of tiles minus the size of the map.
steps: For each dark cell (x, y), loop over corners (a, b) with a in x−1..x and b in y−1..y.
Skip a corner unless 0 ≤ a ≤ m − 2 and 0 ≤ b ≤ n − 2; otherwise add 1 to count[(a, b)].
For each value c in the map, add 1 to tally[c].
pitfalls: Building the whole grid. With m = n = 100 000 that is 10¹⁰ cells.
Letting a cell on the last row or column vote for a corner at m − 1 or n − 1. That tile would hang off the grid.
Packing the corner into one number as a · n + b with 32-bit math. The key can exceed 2³¹; JavaScript numbers and Python ints are fine, Java int is not.

solutions.title: Check every tile
solutions.idea: Put the dark cells in a set and count the dark cells of every tile in the grid.

solutions.title: Let each dark cell vote
solutions.idea: Each dark cell adds one to the at most four tiles that contain it. Only voted tiles are non-empty.

followups: Dark cells are added one at a time and you must report the tally after each addition. What changes per update?
Generalise to k × k tiles. How many tiles does one cell touch now, and when does a 2-D prefix sum become the better tool?
